rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the promise of help came under adverse conditions, God points to winds, layered clouds, and rain as a familiar sign; as rain brings sudden joy, His help for Muhammad will arrive and be welcomed.
rows.anchor: The implication is that in the same manner, God’s mercy and help will appear for Muḥammad (sws).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent repetition distinguishes two moments of lost hope: before rain and before the promised happiness arrived.
rows.anchor: Two separate statements are given here: before rain they had lost hope in rain

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After worldly signs of success, the passage assures believers of mercy in the Hereafter: reviving dead land shows that God will raise the dead, a mercy the deniers foolishly dismiss.
rows.anchor: just as they observe the signs of God’s mercy when He makes the earth lush after it has become dry

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hereafter is a necessary consequence of God’s mercy, whose real purpose is to reward believers for their sacrifices and selfless behaviour.
rows.anchor: the Hereafter is actually a necessary consequence of God’s attribute of mercy

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People quickly despair when rain is delayed and rejoice when it falls, then become ungrateful again when harmful winds pale their crops; only the grateful and patient receive the Prophet’s message.
rows.anchor: generally people despair in a very short while and rejoice in a short while. If there is a little delay in rain, they loose hope

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi distinguishes رياح, mostly favourable or weather-conducive winds, from ريح, generally winds that bring calamities.
rows.anchor: The former is mostly used for favourable winds and winds conducive to the weather. The latter is generally used for winds that bring calamities.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative pronoun in “they see it” refers to زرع, crops, or a similar word; the previous verse’s image of earth reviving supports this antecedent.
rows.anchor: The antecedent of the accusative pronoun in ُہ ۡوَاَرَف is ٌعْرَز or a word of similar meaning.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spiritually dead are fickle people who rapidly swing between despair and arrogance and remain unconvinced despite God’s many signs; the Prophet cannot make them understand, and that is not his responsibility.
rows.anchor: Such people are deaf and blind.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The image suggests even a deaf person might hear when facing the caller, but no response can be expected from those who turn away and run.
rows.anchor: even the deaf could be expected to have some ability to hear if they turn in the direction of the caller

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition ʿan includes the sense of turning away: the Prophet cannot bring the blind back from their errant ways to the right path.
rows.anchor: The implied meaning is that the Prophet (sws) cannot bring the blind back to the right path

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs believed by receptive people are those within and outside human beings, whose evidence of God’s power, mercy, and justice was detailed earlier; unbelievers in these signs cannot be reached by the Prophet’s words.
rows.anchor: those of God’s signs found within and outside human beings towards which attention is directed to with full detail earlier.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who observe and believe the signs around and within them understand the Prophet’s call and submit to God.
rows.anchor: those who observe, understand and believe in the signs around them and those within them will indeed understand

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one should boast of strength or resources: God gives human beings infancy’s weakness, youth’s strength, and old age’s weakness, and alone creates as He wills with full knowledge and power.
rows.anchor: no one should show conceit on his or her strengths, abilities, means and resources. Whatever a person receives is from God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly life should not seem long: wrongdoers will think they remained only an hour when raised, although now they postpone concern through life, death, the barzakh, and resurrection.
rows.anchor: the life of this world should not be regarded as very long. On the Day of Judgement, when the wrongdoers will be raised to life

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing phrase means these foolish people never had a sound estimate of the facts.
rows.anchor: imply that these foolish people never had the inkling

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Judgment Day the past will seem to have vanished in an instant, though in worldly life people considered the stages before resurrection too long to merit concern.
rows.anchor: On the Day of Judgement, they will see as if all their past had vanished in the blink of an eye.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those given knowledge and faith are people whose intellect stayed sound and who knew God’s revelations and believed in God and the Hereafter; they correct wrongdoers by saying the divine register had fixed their stay until Resurrection.
rows.anchor: refers to those people whose intellect remained sound in this world and they were blessed with the knowledge of God’s revelations

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The register of God” means the record in which everything is written.
rows.anchor: refer to the register of God in which everything is written.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about not knowing alludes to people treating the Hereafter as imaginary; those who live mindful of it will face Judgment without anxiety, seeing it as life’s planned destination.
rows.anchor: these people regarded it to be merely a figment of imagination and would not give it any importance.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People who recognize life’s importance and live with the Hereafter in view will not be anxious on Judgment Day; they will see it as the journey’s final destination under God’s plan.
rows.anchor: those who recognize the importance of their life and lead it while keeping the Hereafter in consideration

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wrongdoers’ apologies will not help and they will not get another chance to appease God; preparation must happen in worldly life because the opportunity will not return.
rows.anchor: on that day no person’s apology will be of any avail to him nor will anyone be given the opportunity to try to please his Lord.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi notes that he explained istitab elsewhere; here it denotes a chance to seek God’s favor, which wrongdoers will no longer receive on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: will anyone be given the opportunity to try to please his Lord.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idiom ḍarb mathal originally means offering wise counsel as a parable and, more broadly, simply giving wise counsel.
rows.anchor: The expression ضرب مثل is originally used to convey a wise counsel in the form of a parable

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is told that the Qur’an already contains every needed counsel; if people reject its guidance, disbelievers will call any miracle a lie or trick.
rows.anchor: whatever counsel and advice are needed to make people understand have all been stated in this Qur’ān.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God seals the hearts of those who disable their faculties of understanding and refuse to listen to or grasp what is reasonable.
rows.anchor: God seals the hearts of those who deprive themselves of the faculties of head and heart

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istikhfaf means dismissing someone’s views as flimsy and weak.
rows.anchor: The word استخفاف means to discard the views of someone by regarding them to be flimsy and weak.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing command assures the Prophet to persist: God’s promise of success in this world and the next is certain, and mockers who try to uproot him will themselves fail and be humiliated.
rows.anchor: the promise God has made with him regarding help and success in this world and the next is bound to be fulfilled.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The addressees acknowledge that God created all the things cited above; they are challenged to name anything their other deities created that would justify sharing God’s rights.
rows.anchor: all the above pointed things have been made by God and the addressees of this verse also admit this fact.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the wrongdoers manifestly astray indirectly expresses pity: they have no grounds for treating other deities as God’s partners.
rows.anchor: express pity on such people by addressing them in an indirect way: these people who have transgressed against their souls do not have any reason

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Luqman’s counsel shows Arabs that their own sages taught what the Qur’an teaches; it contrasts blind imitation of forefathers who followed Satan with the wise ancestors’ reflection, and condemns punishing children for conduct Luqman taught his son.
rows.anchor: The succeeding verses refer to the wisdom of Luqmān and the advise he gave to his obedient son.

rows.speaker: some people
rows.claim: Some identify Luqman as Abyssinian, a view Islahi says is incorrect.
rows.anchor: Some people regard him to belong to Abyssinia. However, in my opinion, this is not correct.

rows.speaker: Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Luqman descended from Abraham; Islahi considers this opinion unsound.
rows.anchor: historian Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq says that he belonged to the lineage of Abraham (sws). This opinion also does not seem to be sound.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Poems by the pre-Islamic poets Ṭarfah ibn ‘Abd and Salmā ibn Rabī‘ah indicate that Luqman and his tribe lived in Yemen in grandeur and descended from ‘Ād.
rows.anchor: Among the pre-Islamic jāhiliyyah poets Ṭarfah ibn ‘Abd and Salmā ibn Rabī‘ah have mentioned him and his tribe in their poetry.

rows.speaker: some people
rows.claim: Some people regard Luqman as a prophet; the author’s response is cut off at the end of the segment.
rows.anchor: Some people have regarded Luqmān to be a prophet. However, the opinion of
